titles: Put the creator first, then a bet or question in plain verbs. Never put the result in the title, as 'Red Card', 'Copper' and 'Hang On' did.
Name the guest or opponent when there is one. The only clip with a named guest in the title (Frost Children) got the most views, 21.
Use one or two emoji at the end only.
hooks: Max 6 words, and state what's on the line ('LOSE AND THE STREAM ENDS'), not what happened. Cut hooks that announce the outcome.
Every clip ships with a hook and context line. Check before publishing, since OVl3TBtcYHo and JGopxMMkJo8 shipped with neither.
If the hook and narrator say the same thing, rewrite the hook to add the stake.
clip_picks: Pick moments with a one-line spoken premise (bet, guess, argument, question), and skip visual-only moments like walk-ins, dogs, clinches and boss-fight buildups.
Cut one clip per moment. Four dubstep cuts of one scene is a waste, so keep the named-guest one.
Prioritise Speed or Kai with athletes and celebrities, then Kai with Ray, and run Jynxzi rank guessing as a series with the premise stated in the first line.
length_and_pacing: Stop cutting every clip to 53s. Start ≤2s before the stake line, end ≤2s after the payoff, and aim for 15-30s, since most breakouts run 11-26s.
End on the payoff line and cut trailing banter so the clip loops.
posting: Post 1-2 clips a day within hours of the stream, since clips 5-8 days old sit at 0-15 views.
Confirm scheduled clips actually go public (bj9EzdPPHxI was private).
After 48h, judge on 3s retention and Shorts-feed share. All views are currently 0-21 with n/a analytics, so check Studio for limits, duplicate-content flags and feed serving.
